text:
alex_g: noticing a nasty oscillation on Dedicated pool acme-prod. saw 4 -> 8 -> 4 scale jumps in ~3m and multiple customers reported 429s and timeouts. anyone oncall?

sre_oncall_bot: ALERT: DedicatedPoolAutoscale (acme-prod) flapping. 8 scale events in 1h. rolling error rate 5m=3.8% (>2% threshold). Incident link: https://internal.redwood/c/alerts/4621 :rotating_light:

maria_k: on it. do we have HPA config + any external autoscalers that could conflict? or is this the platform controller?

jordan_p: quick dump of current HPA and scaler state:
```
$ kubectl get hpa -n dedicated acme-prod-scaler -o yaml
minReplicas: 4
maxReplicas: 12
metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        averageUtilization: 60
behavior:
  scaleDown:
    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300
    policies: ...
  scaleUp:
    policies: ...
```
logs show scaleUp at 15:03:02 (4->8), scaleDown at 15:05:10 (8->4). metrics show brief CPU spikes to 85% for ~20s before dropping.

alex_g: also correlating with API errors — p95 latency jumps from 120ms to 800ms during those scale events. I'm seeing prefix cache misses during the cold starts which causes token generation slowdown and client timeouts.

irene_s: this looks classic: short bursts trigger scaleUp, then autoscaler sees lower avg and scales down too fast. two mitigations: increase stabilizationWindowSeconds OR require sustained threshold (hysteresis) using a rolling average. also consider adding a min_stable_instances param to avoid dropping below baseline during bursty traffic.

maria_k: agree. curious if we have multiple controllers (platform autoscaler + k8s HPA) both active? that can cause cascades. jordan, can you check controller logs for duplicated scale requests?

jordan_p: grabbing controller logs now. saw repeated scale commands from platform-controller at 15:03:01 and an HPA evaluation triggered at 15:03:02 — they both executed, resulting in overreaction. rough snippet:
```
[15:03:01] platform-controller: request scale acme-prod -> 8 (reason: latency spike)
[15:03:02] hpa-controller: observed cpu avg=78% -> scaling to 8
```
so double scaling.

alex_g: that's the smoking gun. platform-controller should be the single arbiter. we need coordination or rate-limiting between controllers.

irene_s: short-term fix: bump scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds from 300 -> 900 (5m -> 15m) to avoid immediate downscales. also set scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds=30 and require sustained 30s above threshold. longer term: add a single-source-of-truth gating layer so only one controller authorizes a scale operation per group.

maria_k: customer billing hit: several requests returned 5xx and clients retried causing token usage spikes. billing_bot, can we flag impacted accounts and prepare crediting script?

billing_bot: Found 42 affected API keys between 15:02-15:10. Preparing provisional credits batch id=cr-2026-177900. Need support confirmation.

jordan_p: proposed quick patch (to be tested in staging):
- add 60s rolling avg to cpu metric used by platform-controller
- add 30s minimum sustained over-threshold before scaleUp
- increase scaleDown stabilization to 900s
- introduce controller backoff so it won't apply >1 scale per 60s

irene_s: load-test repro steps I recommend:
```
# from perf lab
hey-load --target 120rps --payload small-chat --duration 5m --route acme-prod
# watch metrics and controller logs
kubectl logs deployment/platform-controller -n platform --since=10m
kubectl get hpa -n dedicated acme-prod-scaler -w
```
we should trigger same burst pattern (short 20-30s high CPU) to validate no double scaling.

alex_g: assigned to @jordan_p and @maria_k for immediate mitigation. I'll open infra PR to change stabilizationWindowSeconds and add controller rate-limit. PR link: https://git.redwood/r/infra/changes/3245 (draft).

maria_k: also will create a customer-facing note and route support tickets for credits. cc @support_lead.

irene_s: additional protective measure: add a small front-door token-bucket limiter per-dedicated-pool to absorb short bursts from noisy tenants. snippet:
```
policies:
  per_pool_rate_limit:
    capacity: 2000
    refill_rate_per_sec: 50
```
this prevents a single tenant from forcing multiple nodes to spin up.

jordan_p: test plan for staging: run hey-load, verify single scaleUp, confirm no 429s or long tail latency spikes, then rollback config if anything regresses.

alex_g: timeline: apply config to staging in 30m, canary to a subset of acme-prod pool after successful staging run, then full roll in 4h window. will notify SRE and Support channels.

maria_k: thanks. action items:
- jordan_p: infra PR + run staging test (ETA 1h)
- alex_g: gatekeeper for canary and rollback plan
- irene_s: prepare rate-limit config and perf-run notes
- billing_bot: finalize credits batch and await approval

jordan_p: noted. will add logs to ticket and paste reproducible commands. :thumbsup:

alex_g: if anyone sees new 429s drop them in this thread with request id. :eyes:

sre_oncall_bot: Command accepted: create incident 2026-177900-autoscale-hysteresis. Pager silence until next update window.

maria_k: closing loop — filed support ticket ref=SUP-9274 and included mitigation steps. will send customer updates once credits approved. :white_check_mark:

irene_s: long-term follow-ups: implement single-scaler arbitration, metric smoothing library in platform-controller, and per-customer QoS guardrails. adding to roadmap.

alex_g: thanks team, will update after staging run.
